[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): All right, thanks everybody for joining. quick roll call, uh, and then Mark will do a quick tech run. we put together an initial POC plan but want to align on success criteria, workloads, and timeline.
[00:18] Priya (Cascade): Thanks Lena. yea, high level — we want to validate Redwood for our customer support assistant and internal ops chat. main goals are latency during peak batch windows and controlling cost per 1k tokens. Also need to prove data isolation for trading desk.
[00:32] Mark (Redwood SE): great. can I ask about the workload shape? qps and token sizes? you had an internal doc earlier but wanna confirm.
[00:40] Priya: sure. baseline: day average QPS ~12, peak QPS ~120 for short bursts, concurrency around 25-40 during peaks. token distribution — about 70% short queries (input 8-40 tokens, output 10-60 tokens), 25% medium (input 200-800, output 200-1000), and 5% long-context (input+context > 8k tokens). these are rough.
[01:05] Mark: okay that distribution is helpful. when you say 8k tokens, is that full KV-sessions or raw context?
[01:10] Priya: that's raw context, we keep rolling KV cache per conversation; some sessions reference long history. for bench we can anonymize and sample.
[01:17] Tom (Cascade Infra): on the infra side we have a VPC in us-east-1 with 25Gbps links and standard egress controls. we can do VPC peering or private link, just need to coordinate maintenance windows.
[01:28] Raj (Security): SOC2 is table stakes. also want to verify KMS integration for key wrapping and audit logs. what does Redwood's private offering look like vs hosted?
[01:38] Lena: good question. Redwood has Hosted API for fastest onboarding, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and Private (VPC/on-prem) for full isolation. for POC we normally do a short Dedicated pilot with VPC peering for secure traffic. we can provide KMS integration and detailed audit logs. we'll share our security pack.
[01:50] Elena (Product): success criteria from product: 95th percentile latency under 300ms for under-128 token exchanges, and for longer multi-turn flows not exceeding 2 seconds for end-to-end response. Also need accuracy/regression checks vs current model outputs.
[02:06] Mark: sounds good. small note — 300ms 95th for <128 tokens is tight depending on model size and quantization. is the expectation cross-request (including network) or server-side only?
[02:16] Elena: user-facing, so end-to-end. includes network.
[02:20] Mark: okay we should factor network in. our Dedicated pools with optimized batching and prefix caching can hit sub-200ms server-side on 7B/13B model families for short responses, but for 70B models it's higher.
[02:33] Priya: we primarily use a 13B open model today in prod; exploring 70B for higher-quality outputs but cost is a concern.
[02:41] Lena: that's very typical. part of POC is to model cost: tokens served, batching, quantization. Mark, can you sketch sizing and recommended instance types for that distribution?
[02:50] Mark: sure. rough back-of-envelope: for 13B quantized int4 on NVIDIA A10/A100-equivalent inference nodes we can do ~120 qps sustained per node for short requests with aggressive batching; concurrency will depend on batching latency target. for mixed distribution with 25% medium and 5% long, we recommend a small fleet of mixed-instance types or model variants: small nodes handling short flows, and larger or pre-warmed instances for long-context ops. also KV cache reduces repeated prefix cost.
[03:20] Priya: what about concurrency cost when many users do long replay simultaneously?
[03:25] Mark: long-context ops are the main cost driver — they tie up GPU memory and compute. for those we recommend setting preemptible burst capacity with larger instances, and fallback policies to a cheaper model if latency SLO would be broken. Redwood supports automated fallback to compatible variants.
[03:40] Tom: what's the expected GPU RAM for 13B int4 vs 70B fp16? approx.
[03:45] Mark: 13B int4 ~20-30GB working set with KV; 70B fp16 around 80-100GB; if you quantize/rewrite kernels maybe lower but plan on 96GB-class instances for 70B. these are approximations — we'll run exact memory profiles during bench.
[03:58] Priya: for the sample data we'll remove any PII but keep tokenization characteristics. is there a preferred format?
[04:04] Lena: CSV with columns timestamp, convo_length_tokens, input_tokens, output_tokens, request_type, and a link to sample JSON payloads. that works well for replay.
[04:12] Priya: ok we'll do that.
[04:16] Elena: curious about continuous batching — how do you balance latency with batching?
[04:20] Mark: we have adaptive batching — we set latency SLO and the runtime dynamically picks batch sizes and scheduling. for short SLOs (100-300ms) batching is more limited, but KV prefix caching helps a lot because repeated prefixes avoid re-compute. also you can use token-limit based micro-batching to control tail latency.
[04:38] Priya: what's the default token window for KV cache?
[04:41] Mark: configurable; many customers use 2-8k rolling window. for your long sessions we can keep the last N tokens in cache and fetch as needed. cache hit rate will determine savings.
[04:52] Raj: encryption at rest specifics — KMS for model keys and TLS for in-flight, do you support HSM for customer-managed keys?
[04:58] Lena: yes, HSM/KMS integrations available on Private and Dedicated, hosted has managed KMS with customer BYOK options in some regions. we'll share the security deck with specifics.
[05:08] Tom: on network egress — do we need to open specific ports? what's the latency overhead for peering vs public?
[05:14] Mark: VPC peering/private link reduces network hop and Jitter — expect lower and more consistent latency. we'll provide network diagrams and maintenance window notes.
[05:21] Priya: about benchmarks — we want to run both synthetic microbench (single prompt repeats) and replay real traffic for 60 minutes. also a cost projection for 30-day run. timeline?
[05:33] Lena: typical POC pattern: week 1 align & prep (share artifacts), week 2 deploy and smoke test, week 3 run benchmarks + iterate, week 4 analysis and go/no-go. we can compress to 3 weeks if you have artifacts ready.
[05:47] Elena: we are aiming for production decision within 4 weeks.
[05:50] Mark: for the benchmark we'll need token distributions and a small sample of actual request latencies so we can replay realistic inter-arrival. For sizing, two calculations we run: 95p latency with target SLO and cost per 1k tokens under expected batching. I can produce a spreadsheet.
[06:07] Priya: that would be great. we want to know expected cost delta if we move from 13B to 70B for the 5% long flows, and if KV cache reduces token compute by 30-50%.
[06:17] Mark: we will model three scenarios: baseline 13B quantized, mixed-mode (13B primary + 70B for long tail), and fallback strategy with cheaper model for heavy tails. we'll show tokens served, GPU hours, and estimated $/1k tokens under those.
[06:30] Lena: any regulatory constraints? data residency?
[06:33] Raj: all production PII must stay in us-east-1 and have audit trails. we might also need an on-prem option for a subset.
[06:41] Mark: Private deployments can run in your VPC or on-prem; for the POC we can simulate private constraints with dedicated pools peered into your environment.
[06:51] Priya: on metrics, what are you going to measure during bench?
[06:54] Mark: latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, model memory growth, cache hit rate, batching stats, and cost breakdown per token (compute, infra, egress). we'll also collect qualitative output diffs vs your prod model for regression detection.
[07:08] Elena: how do you measure output quality? automatic evals?
[07:11] Mark: we can do automated evals on held-out prompts using BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and more importantly your custom success metrics (e.g., answer accuracy rate). human review for a small sample is helpful.
[07:21] Priya: ok. for the replay harness — do you have a recommended tool?
[07:24] Mark: Redwood has an internal runner we can give you access to for POC. we also accept common formats like k6 scripts or JMeter for traffic shaping. usually we prefer our harness since it understands token timing and cache priming.
[07:36] Tom: integration questions — do you support direct S3 import for model artifacts and can you pull from our private registry?
[07:42] Mark: yes, we support private registries and S3-based model artifacts for Private deployments; for hosted we manage the model catalog but can onboard customer models with a secure transfer process.
[07:52] Priya: what about telemetry retention and who sees logs?
[07:55] Lena: telemetry is available in Redwood Console with RBAC; audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM. retention windows vary by plan — we'll include options in the security pack.
[08:05] Raj: can you confirm you capture prompt text in logs? we need ability to redact or mask PII before logs leave our VPC.
[08:13] Mark: yes we have redaction hooks and can do client-side masking; for Private we can enforce never storing raw prompt text in the control plane.
[08:21] Speaker 1 (automatic): [inaudible]...
[08:25] Lena: quick practicals — Priya, can you confirm the sample token CSV delivery date?
[08:29] Priya: will deliver by 2026-03-07, earliest.
[08:33] Lena: Mark, can you produce initial sizing write-up by Monday the 9th?
[08:37] Mark: yep, I'll include QPS-to-GPU mapping and recommended node types and pre-warm strategy.
[08:41] Elena: also, include the benchmark script so we can review.
[08:44] Mark: will do.
[08:46] Priya: for success criteria let's list explicit acceptance: (1) 95p latency < 300ms for short queries end-to-end during 90% of peak load windows; (2) cost per 1k tokens within 15% of our current threshold for day-to-day queries; (3) security checklist satisfied (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 or equivalent); (4) output quality within agreed regression delta.
[09:05] Lena: perfect, we'll codify that in the POC plan.
[09:09] Tom: few nitty-gritty — what's the expected data ingress pattern? bursts or steady?
[09:13] Priya: mostly bursts around morning trading and market close; bursts last 5-20 minutes and can spike 10x baseline.
[09:20] Mark: for spikes we recommend an autoscaling buffer and burst capacity; also pre-warming instances before known windows reduces tail latency.
[09:31] Lena: question from me — are there any hard blackouts during which we cannot run benchmark traffic?
[09:36] Tom: yes, early market open 13:30-14:00 UTC we avoid any testing. outside those times we're okay but will coordinate maintenance windows.
[09:44] Raj: compliance will need a security questionnaire — Lena if you can share the SOC2 and encryption details we'll start the review.
[09:52] Lena: will share security packet by EOD and a link to our SOC2 report.
[09:56] Priya: timeline recap — we want a go/no-go decision by 4 weeks. is that feasible?
[09:59] Mark: yes, with timely artifacts it's feasible. bench during week 3 and analysis week 4.
[10:05] Elena: final ask — include a cost sensitivity chart showing cost vs percent long-context handled by 70B.
[10:12] Mark: will include scenario charts.
[10:15] Lena: recap of next steps: Lena share POC doc + security, Mark sizing + bench scripts, Priya share payloads and token dist, Tom confirm peering window, schedule bench week of 16th. anything else?
[10:27] Priya: no, that's good. thanks everyone.
[10:29] Lena: thanks, we'll follow up via email and add the action items to the CRM.
[10:33] [call ends]
